# rancher_secret_backend (Resource)

Mounts the Rancher secrets engine and writes its connection config. Destroying it unmounts the engine, revoking all of its leases.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "rancher_secret_backend" "rancher" {
  path        = "rancher"
  rancher_url = "https://rancher.example.com"
  ca_cert     = file("${path.module}/rancher-ca.pem")

  request_timeout_seconds = 30
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Mount path for the Rancher secrets engine (e.g. "rancher").
- `rancher_url` (String) Base URL of the Rancher server (e.g. https://rancher.example.com).

### Optional

- `ca_cert` (String) PEM CA certificate that signed the Rancher server's TLS certificate.
- `description` (String) Human-readable description of the mount. Defaults to empty.
- `plugin` (String) Name the plugin is registered under in the plugin catalog. Defaults to `vault-plugin-secrets-rancher`.
- `request_timeout_seconds` (Number) HTTP timeout in seconds for calls from the plugin to Rancher. Defaults to `30`.
- `tls_skip_verify` (Boolean) Skip TLS verification of the Rancher server (not recommended). Defaults to `false`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by mount path. ca_cert is not readable from the engine, so set it in
# configuration after import.
terraform import rancher_secret_backend.rancher rancher
```
